discipline_framing: The commodity-economics foundation of the futures fundamental analyst discipline — agronomy, extraction economics, global supply chain logistics, and production cycles mapped into structural deficit or surplus analysis across the agricultural, energy, and metals complexes that carry a massive portion of CME volume
audience: Aspiring and practicing fundamental analysts of futures markets who need command of the physical-economics of crop, livestock, energy, and metals production — the supply-side literacy that separates genuine fundamental analysis from chart-reading in commodity complexes
sources: The agricultural economics canon (the Gardner and Norton farm-economics traditions, the Alston and Wohlgenant supply-response research, the USDA ERS and university extension publication systems)

The theory of storage and commodity price literature (the Working-Hotelling tradition, the Brennan and Garbade storage models, the convenience-yield research connecting inventories to futures curve shape)
The official balance-sheet methodology (the USDA WASDE construction system, the FAO and IGC crop accounting frameworks, the EIA and IEA energy balance traditions)

The energy economics literature (the petroleum economics tradition from Adelman through the modern shale-cycle research, the natural gas market structure studies, the extraction-economics and Hotelling-rule lineage)
The mining and metals economics tradition (the Mikesell and Tilton mineral-economics lineage, the grade-decline and discovery-cycle literature, the smelting and refining economics studies)

The global logistics and freight economics literature (the maritime economics canon including the Stopford tradition, the grain and container logistics systems, the pipeline and rail economics of North American energy)
The futures market structure documentation (CME Group rulebooks and contract specifications, the cash-market and basis literature from the agricultural extension tradition)
pitfalls: Weather-narrative-without-balance-sheet — treating every rainfall headline as a price driver while ignoring where stocks sit and how much of the crop is already made, letting stories override arithmetic
Elasticity-uniformity — applying one supply-response logic across commodities whose production cycles run from six weeks (broilers) to ten years (mines), producing systematically wrong horizon calls
Storage-blindness — reading flat prices without the carry, inventories, and convenience yields that explain why the curve looks the way it does and what it signals about physical tightness
Logistics-free analysis — modeling global balances as if commodities teleport, missing the freight, basis, and chokepoint dynamics that decouple regional prices from world prices

Cycle-phase confusion — reading high prices as a demand event when the capital-investment cycle of production response is mid-turn, then getting run over by the supply wave that high prices already commissioned
